public_payload.normalized_proposition: When the AI bubble pops and capex falls, layoffs and offshoring will accelerate, driven partly by tech companies needing to show fiscal restraint for the first time in living memory.
conditions: when the AI bubble pops and capex falls

statement.excerpt: Expect to see an acceleration in layoffs and offshoring, in part driven by a need for tech companies to show — for the first time in living memory — fiscal restraint.

from_speaker: an acceleration in layoffs and offshoring
in part driven by a need for tech companies
for the first time in living memory
our_interpretation: The preceding paragraph makes this a forecast conditional on an AI bust and a substantive capex decline. That condition comes from context, not the quoted sentence alone.
The ordinary reading requires both layoffs and transfers of work abroad to increase across the technology sector relative to comparable pre-downturn periods.
Fiscal restraint must contribute to those changes; the claim does not require it to be the sole cause.

I read 'for the first time in living memory' as rhetorical emphasis within the forecast. It has no defined historical boundary, and this assessment does not endorse it as a separate historical finding.
The surrounding discussion of US markets and technology cities makes US technology employment the principal geographic scope.
criteria.support_condition: After an independently documented AI bust and capex decline, comparable records show accelerated technology layoffs and offshoring, with corporate disclosures or credible analysis linking part of both changes to fiscal restraint.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The antecedent occurs, but adequate follow-up shows that a required trend did not accelerate or that the claimed fiscal-restraint contribution was absent. Changes before an established trigger do not settle this conditional forecast.

evidence.explanation: Technology layoff announcements increased over the comparable prior-year period, consistent with the layoff component considered alone. The report does not establish that an AI capex bust preceded the increase, measure offshoring, or establish the specified causal chain.

evidence.explanation: The cross-industry survey describes outsourcing alongside technology investment and multiple business motives. It cannot establish accelerated technology-sector offshoring caused by restraint after an AI bust.
